evidence: The published Definition was inspected: it supplies exact operator application v->Av and vector additions/scalar multiples without requiring stored matrix entries. The algorithm applies that interface to P=I+Q/nu. It claims no CSR representation/cost, arithmetic stability, or Krylov convergence.

Facts F1 and Verification 1.1–1.3 instantiate E=N0, two increments +/-1, rates 1,n; the death rate is zero at zero and total rate 1+n is finite. QV=1-n is used under the separately declared choice/nonexplosion theorem. Operator-on-functions convention is kept separate from the explicitly column-oriented cemetery matrix.
review_scope: Actual supplier Statement/Definition to consumer Facts/Proof/Definition/use; interface compatibility only, not whole-item independent acceptance.

evidence: The complete current theorem Statement and Proof and its Step 1 ready record were inspected. The required interface is: under Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, a finite-channel process with a proper V>=1 and local QV<=cV is nonexplosive. For immigration/death, V(n)=1+n has finite sublevel sets and QV(n)=1-n<=V(n) for every n>=0; the death channel has zero propensity at n=0, all total rates 1+n are finite, and positive-propensity poststates lie in N0. The cited record is authoring readiness only, not independent approval.

The current batch-28 page and complete global error theorem/proof were inspected. Its recurrence requires uniform local defect, one-step stability, a fixed grid, and a common compact tube; none is used here. This pair contains no global ODE or density discretization estimate, so the page is design context only.

The actual published Markov-kernel/chain page and the exact kernel-composition suppliers were inspected. This pair assumes a given time-homogeneous countable chain with its semigroup and nonexplosion as inputs; it does not construct a chain from an arbitrary countable rate array. The initial-distribution definition is deliberately not imported, so its Choice dependency is not added to the choice-free core arguments.

The current published page and the exact induced-norm statements/proofs were inspected. The local matrix-exponential series and truncation arguments use the induced 1-norm, compatibility/submultiplicativity, and the max-column-sum formula under the nonempty finite-matrix hypotheses. No conditioning, floating-point stability theorem, or convergence result is imported.

The current batch-7 page and full forward-Euler local-consistency theorem/proof were inspected. Its hypotheses concern local ODE defect and one-step Lipschitz stability. No forward-Euler or time-discretization estimate is used in this exact finite matrix-exponential/uniformization pair; the page remains declared design context only.

The published Poisson page and exact suppliers def-scalar-poisson-count-law and lem-poisson-count-law-normalization-and-moments were inspected. Their finite-parameter mass formula and normalization are the only imported count-law facts; the geometric right-tail estimate is proved locally, including the zero-parameter case.

The current batch-2 page and complete relevant CSR definition, exact matvec, and cost statements/proofs were inspected. They establish stored-entry representation and exact-arithmetic operation/storage counts only. This pair makes no CSR cost, finite-precision CSR stability, or Krylov convergence claim and does not use the CSR theorem as a premise.

The current batch-10 page and the full nonexplosion theorem/proof were inspected. The theorem is used only in the immigration-death example, under its finite-channel reaction hypotheses, admissible positive-propensity poststates, proper V(n)=1+n, QV<=V, and explicit Countable Choice plus Dependent Choice branch. Other countable-chain results assume a given nonexplosive process.
